stops.teaser: A capitol with no dome, built partly with iron, and an architect buried in its walls.

story: Architect William Strickland of Philadelphia designed the capitol and thought it was his greatest achievement. It was built between 1845 and 1859 by skilled artisans and by convict and slave labor. It has been used continuously since 1853.

It was built mostly of limestone quarried nearby, and it was one of the first buildings in the United States to use iron as a structural element. It is one of eleven state capitols with no dome. When it was completed it was the tallest building in the southeastern United States. Its cupola is modeled on the Choragic Monument of Lysicrates.

During the Civil War the building was a camp for Union troops, a hospital and a lookout. Strickland, who died before it was finished, and Samuel Morgan, who oversaw construction, are entombed in its walls. The tombs of President James K. Polk and his wife are on the grounds.
stops.fact: It is one of eleven capitols with no dome.
stops.disputed: Many people think every statehouse has a dome. Wikipedia says eleven do not, including this one.

claims.t: The Tennessee State Capitol has been used continuously since 1853.
The capitol has a large dome.
claims.why: It is one of eleven state capitols with no dome.

spot.q: Tennessee's Capitol is one of eleven state capitols missing something. What?
spot.why: It is one of eleven state capitols with no dome. Its cupola is modeled on the Choragic Monument of Lysicrates.

story: Nashville's Union Station was built starting in 1898 and opened on October 9, 1900. Richard Montfort planned it, in the Romanesque style of Henry Hobson Richardson, who is also credited. Montfort was an engineer for the Louisville and Nashville Railroad and spent several years planning the building.

The building is Romanesque Revival, a look that stood out among train stations of the time. It was built west of downtown and next to a viaduct. Streetcars used it too, until streetcars ended in Nashville in 1941. It became a National Historic Landmark in 1975.

The last passenger trains left in the late 1970s. After it was abandoned for several years, the station reopened in 1986 as the Union Station Hotel. In 2012 it became a Marriott Autograph Collection hotel.

stops.disputed: Many people think a station this old must be a ruin or a museum. Wikipedia says it is a working hotel.

stops.clue: Go to the Public Square in downtown Nashville. Look for a big tan stone building with tall narrow windows and DAVIDSON COUNTY carved across the top.
stops.safety: Downtown streets are busy. Use crosswalks and stay on the sidewalks.

story: In 1784, Thomas Molloy platted Nashville and set aside a four-acre parcel on the bluffs as a civic space. That space became the Public Square, and more than one courthouse has stood on it.

The 1892 photograph shows the Courthouse and Market on the square, crowded with horses and wagons. The current courthouse was built in 1936-37 with federal funds, designed by Emmons H. Woolwine with Hirons and Dennison of New York.

It is an eight-story, steel-frame Art Deco building covered in Indiana limestone. It was the first building in Davidson County with central air conditioning. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1987 and today holds the offices of the mayor and the Metro Council.
stops.fact: It was the first building in Davidson County with central air conditioning.
stops.disputed: Pages about the square disagree on how many courthouses stood here. One calls the current building the fifth on these grounds, while another record lists three earlier buildings.

story: The Parthenon in Centennial Park is a full-scale replica of the Parthenon in Athens. William Crawford Smith designed it, and it was built in 1897 for the Tennessee Centennial Exposition. Nashville's nickname, the "Athens of the South," influenced the choice.

Wikipedia says it was the only building at the Exposition that was an exact reproduction. It was built of plaster, wood and brick and was not meant to last, but it was so popular that it was left standing. After weather damaged it, it was rebuilt in concrete, with the exterior finished in 1925 and the interior in 1931.
Inside, Alan LeQuire's 1990 re-creation of the Athena Parthenos statue is the focus of the building. It is now an art museum.
stops.fact: The first one was made of plaster.
stops.disputed: Many people think the building is ancient or even made of marble. Wikipedia says the first was plaster, wood and brick, and the current one is concrete.

spot.q: The Parthenon was built in 1897 and was not meant to last. Why is it still standing?
options: It was meant as a permanent museum from the start
The city won it in a lawsuit
It was so popular that it was left standing, then rebuilt in concrete
spot.why: It was built of plaster, wood and brick for the Tennessee Centennial Exposition, but it was so popular it was left standing. After weather damaged it, it was rebuilt in concrete.
